secure-wipe: add wipe_disk function This CL is a part of Full Disk Wipe project. We aim to provide users with the functionality to securely and throughly wipe their device if they want to. - wipe_disk script added to perform full disk wipe for the device. This will be called via chroot from recovery. - perform_fio_op is modified to be able to verify the disk is zeroed. - Added sanitize support to secure_erase_nvme. Nvme sanitize, if supported, is preferred over nvme format because nvme sanitize guarantees physical data destruction. recovery: add full disk wipe functionality to recovery With this functionality, users will be able to erase their device thoroughly and securely during recovery. The full disk wipe process is triggered by "space" key press in the beginning of the recovery. Also, a small UI is added to inform users about the progress and the result of the full disk wipe. This feature will not be enabled in beta and stable channels for now because we haven't decided on the final UX design yet. TEST=Tested manually on sata, mmc and nvme devices by starting recovery, triggering the full disk wipe by pressing space and seeing the logs after recovery ends. camera: usb_v1: Remove usage of /dev/camera-internal* symlinks The /dev/camera-internal* symlinks are created by the udev rule file 50-camera.rules. But in the newer kernel, there is a metadata device node for each UVC camera, and it's indistinguishable by built-in udev rule without running an external program. The symlinks are used for two purposes: 1. To have a static device path across suspend/resume cycle. 2. Filter out external camera. This CL removes the usage of /dev/camera-internal* and uses /dev/v4l/by-path/* instead, which is also persistent across suspend/resume. The external camera is filtered out by checking whether it's presented in camera_characteristics.conf. UPSTREAM: ath6kl: add some bounds checking The "ev->traffic_class" and "reply->ac" variables come from the network and they're used as an offset into the wmi->stream_exist_for_ac[] array. Those variables are u8 so they can be 0-255 but the stream_exist_for_ac[] array only has WMM_NUM_AC (4) elements. We need to add a couple bounds checks to prevent array overflows. I also modified one existing check from "if (traffic_class > 3) {" to "if (traffic_class >= WMM_NUM_AC) {" just to make them all consistent.
